appraisal_events.evidence: Écriture... simplement besoin d’être lue à rebours; «Il serait possible que j’aille demain chez les Verdurin...», anagramme enfantin de cet aveu: «J’irai demain chez les Verdurin, c’est absolument certain...»; Albertine employait toujours le ton dubitatif pour les résolutions irrévocables.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator's confident decoding of Albertine's hesitant phrasing as a settled, concealed intention frames her as habitually deceptive, diminishing her trustworthiness within his account.

appraisal_events.evidence: J’avais sans doute hérité de mon père ce brusque désir arbitraire de menacer les êtres que j’aimais le plus... je disais négligemment, pour la faire trembler, que je comptais sortir ce jour-là.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator explicitly exposes his own inherited, arbitrary impulse to control and frighten Albertine, a self-implicating admission of tyrannical jealousy.

status_effects.explanation: Albertine is locally cast as a practiced, calculated liar through the narrator's close reading of her phrasing.
The narrator's own admission of manipulative, inherited jealousy locally diminishes him by exposing his controlling behavior toward Albertine.

ambiguities: The passage's account of Albertine's lying is entirely the narrator's own jealous interpretive reconstruction; the text does not independently confirm the deception, so the diminishment of Albertine rests on an unreliable, self-interested narrating voice.
